test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-II Official Paper-I (Held On: 20 Jan, 2025)
subject: general
question: What is the central theme of the passage describing the extraction process of indigo dye from the Indigofera plant?

options.text: The cultivation and growth cycle of the Indigofera plan
The various uses of indigo dye in different industries
The impact of lime and natural sugars on the indigo extraction process
The intricate process of harvesting and processing indigo leaves

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage provides a comprehensive, sequential account of how indigo is produced, starting from the **harvesting** of the leaves to the final **drying** of the dye cakes.
 
• While other elements are mentioned (like lime or irrigation), they are secondary details within the broader framework of the **processing steps**.
 
• The text covers harvesting, soaking, churning, settling, filtering, compressing, and drying—which collectively define the **intricate process** of turning a plant into a usable dye.
 
• Options 1, 2, and 3 focus on specific sub-details or outside contexts, whereas **Option 4** captures the entirety of the narrative's focus.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Summary from Text:** *"The extraction of indigo dye involves **harvesting**... **soaking**... **churning**... **filtration**... **compression** into cakes and **drying**..."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: Cultivation and growth cycle** – The passage only mentions harvesting before flowers bloom; it does not discuss how to plant or grow the crop.
 
• **Option 2: Various uses in industries** – The text only says it is "ready for use as a dye," without listing specific industrial applications like textiles or ink.
 
• **Option 3: Impact of lime and sugars** – These are mentioned only at the very end as additives to "enhance" the process, not as the primary subject of the entire text.
